First-time setup, run once per load: $01=$25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000), load the font file $0F to $6800 ($1239), load and unpack the ramp picture (load_ramp_picture), load the pose and sprite data files $11 and $12 (load_skater_data), then NOP out the JMP at $0880 and fall into hj_init.

Per-entry initialisation: SEI, $01=$25, wait for the frame wrap ($0A45), black border and background, $D011=$2B (bitmap mode with the display blanked), clear zero page $12-$72 ($1304), build the quarter-square table at $0400-$07FF ($1310), build the bit-reversal tables at $2E7B/$2F7B ($1340), $1AFA, set up bitmap video and colour RAM (init_bitmap_video), the header row and sprites (init_header_and_sprites), the raster interrupt (install_raster_irq), the sound driver ($22B7) and the event state ($19C3: pass count $3A=0, one of two sprite colour schemes at random, phase 0), then CLI into the main loop.

Main loop, outside the interrupt; never returns (the event leaves through JMP $FE06 at $1A93). If $6F is set (the Commodore key turned sound off, $1A24) re-run the sound initialiser $22B7 and clear $6F. If the sound-request ring's read index $71 differs from its write index $70, take the next request ($1AA5) and pass it to the sound queue ($22F5). If the tick count $72 (raised once a frame at $0B31) is nonzero, run one step of the sound driver ($232C) and decrement it.

Load file $10 to $4000 (resident loader, X/Y = load address) and keep the end address it returns in $16/$17; run-length unpack $4000..end into $7000 ($1B6A); then copy the unpacked picture out with copy_block: $1F40 bitmap bytes to $4000, $3E8 screen-matrix bytes to $6400 and $3E8 colour bytes to $6000, which init_bitmap_video copies into colour RAM on every entry.

Load file $11 to $7000 and keep the end address the loader returns in $2E61/$2E62, then load file $12 straight after it (X/Y still hold that end). The loader table at $F2F9 gives lengths $1284 and $402C, so the files fill $7000-$8283 and $8284-$C2AF. $7000 is the base of the 30-byte pose records that set_pose_pointer indexes.

The address the reset vector $FFFC holds, inside load_skater_data (STY $2E62 / LDA #$12 / JSR $F230 / RTS). High Jump never writes $FFFC; the boot code at $03AB-$03B8 stored $0954 in both $FFFA/$FFFB and $FFFC/$FFFD, and the town snapshot already held it.

Point $29/$2A at pose record A: $7000 + A*30, with the 8x8-bit multiply at $136A (quarter squares). Each record holds five 6-byte sprite parts; byte 3 of a part is its X offset and byte 4 its Y offset (place_part_sprite). Called from place_sprites ($0BB1, $0BC9, $0BFF) and from $14F7, $1524, $1548.
Add A to the 16-bit pointer $12/$13. Not called in this load: no instruction names $096D and the word $096D occurs nowhere in the 64 KB image.

Header row and sprite set-up, part 1: CIA 1 port A outputs ($7F, keyboard row 7) and port B inputs ($FF); copy the random seed byte $2E5F to $2E60; copy 40 colour bytes from $2D8F into the top row of the screen matrix at $6400; print the inline text at $09A1 ('PASS:' and 'HEIGHT:') into bitmap row 0 at $4000 through $1242, which returns to $09CA.

Inline text for JSR $1242 at $099E: 40 ASCII bytes and a zero terminator ($09C9), 16 spaces, 'PASS:', 4 spaces, 'HEIGHT:', 8 spaces. $1242 masks each byte with $3F and draws that glyph of the $6800 font, inverted, into bitmap row 0, then returns to $09CA. Data, not code: decoded as instructions it would read JSR $2020 and JSR $4150. Never disassemble a range containing $099E.

Header row and sprite set-up, part 2 (after the inline text): print the string the resident code points to at $FE00/$FE01 (in this snapshot $F822, 'PRACTICE') at the start of bitmap row 0; sprite page $22=$B0; sprite multicolours $D025=1 and $D026=6; colour mask $45=$FF; copy the colour byte $FE02 into entry 4 (sprite 4) of both sprite colour schemes, $2D83 and $2D8B; starting pose $4F=$2A35[0]; build the skater sprites ($14DE); copy the two 64-byte ruler shapes $2CFF and $2D3F to $6D40 and $6D80 (sprite pointers $B5 and $B6).

Board colour: copy the skater attribute $FE02 (event manager slot A; 7 for every roster skater, $0D for LESTER) into entry 4 of both sprite colour sets, $2D83 and $2D8B, so sprite 4 (the board) takes it whichever set $19D3 picks.
Copy the two 64-byte height-ruler sprites from $2CFF/$2D3F to sprite blocks $B5/$B6 ($6D40/$6D80), shown as sprites 5 and 6.

Install the raster interrupt: SEI, $01=$25, CIA 1 interrupts off ($DC0D=$7F, then read to acknowledge), wait for the frame wrap ($0A45), band $1E=0, clear the raster compare's bit 8, first compare line from $2A05 ($F9), IRQ vector $FFFE/$FFFF = $0AF0, enable the raster interrupt. The NMI vector at $FFFA holds $0A3A, the middle of this routine (LDA #$0A / STA $FFFF / LDA #$01 / STA $D01A / RTS); this load never writes $FFFA, and the vector already held $0A3A in the town snapshot.

The address the NMI vector $FFFA holds, inside install_raster_irq: from here LDA #$0A / STA $FFFF / LDA #$01 / STA $D01A / RTS, not an interrupt handler (it ends in RTS, not RTI). High Jump never writes $FFFA; the same $0A3A was already there in the town snapshot, a value left by an earlier load.

Wait until the raster line's low byte ($D012) falls, which happens when a new frame starts (PAL line $137 to 0); the 255-to-256 step reads as $FF to $00, which CMP sees as an increase, so it does not end the wait.

Bitmap video set-up: black border and background, copy $3E8 colour bytes from $6000 into colour RAM $D800 (copy_block), $D018=$90 (screen matrix $2400 and bitmap $0000 within the bank), $DD00 bits 0-1 = %10 (VIC bank 1, so $6400 and $4000), $D016=$18 (multicolour, 40 columns), $D011=$3B (bitmap mode, display on, 25 rows, Y scroll 3). Returns with carry clear.

Copy Y*256+X bytes from the read pointer $12/$13 to the write pointer $14/$15, advancing both (read_ptr12_byte, write_ptr14_byte); $18/$19 count down the low and high parts. Used by load_ramp_picture and init_bitmap_video.

Unreferenced: like copy_block but takes each byte from JSR $FFCF (CHRIN in the KERNAL jump table). No instruction or pointer names $0AA2 in this load (the two $0A,$A2 byte pairs at $1B02 and $1B30 are LDX #$0A / LDY #$00 and LDX #$0A / LDY #$07), and with $01=$25 the KERNAL is banked out, so $FFCF would run RAM. Library code carried in the program, not used by High Jump.
Unreferenced: write Y*256+X zero bytes through the write pointer $14/$15 (write_ptr14_byte). Nothing in the image names $0ABA (instruction and word scan).
Return the byte at ($12) in A and advance the pointer $12/$13; leaves Y=0. Byte source for copy_block, the run-length unpacker $1B6A and the inline-text printer $1242.
Store A at ($14) and advance the pointer $14/$15; leaves Y=0. Byte sink for copy_block, fill_block_zero, copy_block_from_ffcf and the unpacker $1B6A.

Unreferenced: JSR $FFE7 (CLALL in the KERNAL table), then repeat JSR $FFE4 (GETIN) until it returns a nonzero key. Nothing in the image names $0AE7, and with the KERNAL banked out ($01=$25) those addresses hold RAM.

Raster interrupt entry (vector $FFFE): push A, X, Y; acknowledge $D019; take the handler for band $1E from the word table $2A01 ($0B21 for band 0, $0CA3 for band 1), patch it into the JSR operand at $0B0C/$0B0D and call it; then move $1E to the next band from $2A07 (0 to 1 to 0) and set the next compare line from $2A05 (band 0 at line $F9, band 1 at line $37). Two interrupts a frame.
Low byte of the band handler's address in JSR $0CA3, rewritten every interrupt at $0B02 from $2A01+2*$1E.
High byte of the band handler's address in the same JSR, rewritten every interrupt at $0B08 from $2A02+2*$1E.

Band 0 handler, raster line $F9 (below the picture): clear $D016's multicolour bit and set $D011=$33 so the next frame begins with the header row in hires bitmap; count the frame in $2C/$2D ($15E3); add a sound tick to $72 for the main loop; position and colour the sprites (place_sprites); poll RUN/STOP ($1A08, which ends the event through $1A49) and the Commodore key ($1A24, sound on and off); every fourth frame (low two bits of $2C zero) decrement $40, or $3F once $40 is zero; then one random redraw of a picture cell at a 1-in-8 chance ($199B), otherwise two tries of $19AE, whose chance grows with $3F.

Set the sprites for the frame. Enable sprites 0-4 plus the bits in $66; no priority or X expansion; Y-expand sprites 5 and 6 ($D017=$60); multicolour for sprites 1, 2, 5 and 6 where $45 allows ($D01C = $66 AND $45). Pointers at $67F8: sprites 0-4 take $22..$22+4, sprite 7 takes $22+4 as well, sprites 5 and 6 take $B5 and $B6. Colour of sprite n: $2E63+n when bit n of $45 is set, else 0 (black). Positions: when $25 bit 7 is set (the fall, phase 6) sprites 0-3 come from pose $5F at $59/$5A/$5B, mirrored by the side bit $58, and sprite 4 from the fifth part of the skater pose $4F; otherwise sprites 0-4 are the five parts of pose $4F at $49/$4A/$4B, mirrored by the side bit $48 (place_part_sprite). Sprites 5 and 6 go to fixed places (place_fixed_sprite). Sprite 7 copies sprite 4's X and sits at sprite 4's Y + $69 - $4B + 1; with colour 0 in both schemes it reads as a shadow. $D010 is built from the bits gathered in $1B.
Sprites 5 and 6 always show blocks $B5 and $B6, the height ruler copied there at start-up ($0A01).

Position sprite $18 (register offset $19 = 2*$18) from the pose part at ($29): Y = $6C + part byte 4; X = $6A/$6B + part byte 3 when the side byte $1A has bit 7 set (right half of the ramp), or $6A/$6B minus byte 3 otherwise ($0C6F), which mirrors the figure about its origin; the X high bit is rotated into $1B for $D010.

Position sprite $18 from fixed-table entry Y (0 or 1): Y coordinate from $2E05, X low byte from $2E01, X high bit from bit 0 of $2E03 rotated into $1B. The two entries place sprites 5 and 6, the tick-marked ruler shapes, at X=320 and Y=60 and 102, one Y-expanded sprite above the other.

Band 1 handler, raster line $37: busy-wait for line $3A, then set $D016's multicolour bit and $D011=$3B so the ramp picture shows in multicolour bitmap. Then the frame's game update: read the controls and run the current phase (read_controls_and_run_phase); keep the best height in $2B ($1AB4); clamp the scale $51/$52 ($1856); if the side bit $48 differs from last frame's $20 (the skater crossed the middle of the ramp), set $37=$FF and $26=1 and, when $25 and $43 are clear, $3A=4 and the skater is now on the right half, request sound 4 ($1A96); rebuild the skater sprite graphics ($14DE) when the side, the pose $4F or (falling) the pose $5F changed; save $4F, $48, $5F in $1F, $20, $21; copy $32 to $39; set $66 ($19F8); then run $19AE until raster line $DC or ten times.

Read the controls: $DC01 (joystick port 1) AND $DC00 (joystick port 2) into $2F, active low, bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire. Port A drives $7F, so keyboard row 7 also reaches $DC01: SPACE reads as fire, 1 as up, the left-arrow key as down, CTRL as left and 2 as right. $30 = new OR NOT old, so a bit of $30 is 0 only on the frame its line goes from released to pressed. While $43 is set, bits 0 and 1 of $30 are forced to 0. Then jump to the handler for phase $2E through the word table $2AB9, patched into the JMP at $0D4D.
Low byte of the phase handler's address in the JMP at $0D4D, rewritten at $0D44 from $2AB9+$2E on every call.
High byte of the phase handler's address in the JMP at $0D4D, rewritten at $0D4A from $2ABA+$2E.

Phase 0, standing on the platform: clear $25 (not falling) and the timers $3F/$40, colour mask $45=$FF, ramp position $54/$55=$0056 (left platform) turned into $46/$47 and the side bit $48 by $12A0. While the counters $31/$32 are both zero and fire has not just been pressed, start the fidget animation (phase $0C, variant $33 = random 0 or 1) with a 4-in-256 chance per frame ($15DA with $55 returns 0 for random values 0-3). Once fire is pressed the push-off runs: $31 counts six frames per step of $32, ten steps (60 frames), pose $4F=$2A35[$32]; at the end phase 2 begins ($1130 sets the start position from the side bit), the speed $4D/$4E comes from $1921 ($0080 on the left, $FF80 on the right), $37=2, $24=0, and the new phase runs at once (JMP $0D23).

Phase $0C, the fidget animation on the platform: keep the start position ($12A0) and display coordinates ($117B). If fire has just been pressed, go back to phase 0 and run it at once, which starts the push-off. Otherwise $31 counts six frames per step of $32; the pose $4F is $2A9F[$32] for variant $33=0 or $2AAB[$32] for variant 1; when $32 reaches $2AB7[$33] (12 for both) the counters clear and phase 0 resumes.

Phase 2, riding the ramp: move along it ($114D), apply the speed ($16BC), ramp sounds ($1722), and when the vertical coordinate $23 is $B0 or more (the low part of the ramp) the pump input ($16E3: a direction just pressed adds speed). While $23 is $96 or more (below the rim) the pose comes from the first triple at $2A17 whose threshold exceeds $23: its second byte, or its third when $24 bit 7 is set; a negative entry means pose $2A09[$37] (or $2A0D[$37] with $24 set), after $1798 resolves $37 if it is $FF. When $23 drops below $96 the skater leaves the ramp: $42 = bit 7 of $4E, and the next phase is $2A11[$37], 4 (in the air) for $37=0 or $0E (the closing sequence) for $37=1.

Phase 6, a fall: $25=$FF, so place_sprites draws the fallen figure from pose $5F and leaves the board (sprite 4) on the skater pose $4F. $1834 then $18B1 or $187D, movement ($114D, $16BC), board pose from the second bytes of the $2A17 triples by $23 (negative: $2A09[0]). While $33=0 the figure's own motion runs ($14C3, $117F with X=$10) and its pose $5F follows its height $57 through the thresholds at $2A4D, until $57 reaches $F0 ($57 and $33 set to $F0). Then the lying-down animation: $31 counts eight frames per step of $32 up to $2A6F[$27] steps (6 for $27=0, 12 for $27=1, chosen at $1684 by the speed); $5F from $2A63, or for $27=0 from $2A57 with the colour mask $45 from $2A5D; $56 += $2A71[$27]. After it, a new press of fire returns to the platform (phase 0), or, once five passes are counted ($3A>=5), starts phase $10 with $51/$52=$00F8.

Phase 4, in the air: spin control (air_spin_control, active only while $43 is set), movement ($114D), and $1AD0, which counts a pass when the sign of the speed $4E flips while the skater is on the right half ($48 bit 7). Above the rim ($23 < $96): with fire held ($2F bit 4 low) on the right half, pose 8 starts the seven-pose sequence at $2A3F and pose $10 the one at $2A46 ($1C/$1D, the pose saved in $35), as phase 8. Back at the rim ($23 >= $96) it lands: $24 = $FF when the pose, folded into 0-$17, is $0C-$13, else 0; if the pose's low three bits are 0, 1 or 7 the run continues in phase 2, otherwise $1115 starts a fall (phase 6).

Spin control in the air, only while $43 is set (else returns at once). A new press of left ($30 bit 2) toggles $33 between $00 and $40 (air_spin_left_press); a new press of right (bit 3) sets $33=$60 (air_spin_right_press). With $33 bit 6 set, bit 5 picks the direction: air_spin_step_a or air_spin_step_b adds or subtracts $59 in the fraction $27 and, on each carry or borrow, counts $28 and steps the pose $4F one place, wrapping $07-$17 and $18-$27 within their groups of 16.
Left just pressed in the air: if $33 bit 5 is set clear $33, otherwise set $33=$40.
Right just pressed in the air: set $33=$60 (the $00 written first when bit 5 was clear is overwritten at once).

Spin step for $33=$40: on the left half ($48 bit 7 clear), add $59+1 to $27; on carry count $28 and step the pose back one ($4F-1, $17 wrapping to $27 and $07 to $17). On the right half it runs the opposite step (air_spin_step_b from $0FE4).

Spin step for $33=$60: on the left half ($48 bit 7 clear), subtract $59+1 from $27 (carry is clear); on borrow count $28 and step the pose forward ($4F+1, $28 wrapping to $18 and $18 to $08). On the right half it runs air_spin_step_a's add at $0FC0 instead.
Tail of the in-air pose stepper at $0FBC/$0FE0: store the stepped skater pose X in $4F. The RTS at $1003 is also that stepper's exit when the $27 sub-counter does not carry.

Phase $08, trick wind-up (entered from phase $04 when fire is held in the air on the right half with pose $08 or $10; $1C/$1D point at $2A3F or $2A46): move the skater ($114D), apply friction ($16BC), check for a turnaround ($1AD0); dropping to the coping ($23 >= $96) bails through $1115. Every second tick $32 steps through seven poses at ($1C) into $4F; after the seventh, phase $0A.

Phase $0A, trick held and released: while $31/$32 are both zero (the first tick, and every tick fire stays held, $2F bit 4 low) set the height bonus $44 = 4 and count $27; then step the seven poses at ($1C) in reverse every second tick. Dropping to the coping ($23 >= $96) bails ($1115). At the end restore pose $35, set $33 = $60 if $27 >= $14 (held too long: the pose spins in $0F78) else 0, lock the controls ($43 = $FF) and return to phase $04.

Phase $0E, run over (phase $02 reached the coping with $37 = 1: controls locked or five passes): every sixth tick step $32 through seven poses from $2A73, or $2A7A when $24 is negative; after the seventh, phase $10.

Phase $10, final pose on the platform: clear $25, set $45 = $FF, queue sound 6 on the first tick, step $32 every ten ticks up to 9, keep the skater placed from $54 ($12A0, $117B) and take the pose from $2A81 (height $2B < $50, under 10 ft), $2A8B (< $68, under 13 ft) or $2A95 (13 ft or more). Once $32 is 9, a newly pressed fire ends the event through $1A49.

Bail: enter phase $06 with the path position put back to the platform for the current side ($1132), set velocity $4D/$4E to $0080 or $FF80 ($1921), and jump back into the input and phase dispatch at $0D23 so phase $06 runs in this same frame. Reached from phase $04 (a bad landing pose) and phases $08/$0A (reaching the coping mid-trick).

No caller found (byte scan for JSR/JMP operands, little-endian words, address-minus-one words and immediate lo/hi pairs); it follows the JMP at $1121, so nothing falls into it. Would enter phase $06 at the platform position ($1132) with velocity $4D/$4E zeroed.
Start a run (phase $00 at $0D89, after its countdown): set phase $02 and fall into $1132/$1135, putting the skater at the platform position.
Set the phase to A through set_highjump_phase, then fall into place_skater_on_platform. Called by bail_to_phase_06 with A = 6.
Put skater 0's path position $54/$55 on the platform of the current side: $0056 when $48 bit 7 is clear (left half), $01CC ($222 - $56) when set. Also called by set_highjump_phase for phase $10.
Motion step for skater 0 (X = 0), called by phases $02, $04, $06, $08 and $0A: continues at $1154.
No caller found (same scan as $1124): the motion step for object 1 (X = $10, fields $56-$65). It takes the X <> 0 path at $115C straight to $117F, skipping the height caps.

Integrate velocity and slope ($146F), look up the ramp coordinates ($12A0), copy height $47 to $23 (before the caps); unless $25 is negative, cap the height at the coping ($96) when $2A13[$37] is nonzero (the run is heading back to a platform); hold $47 at $16 or more; then fall into compute_skater_display_position.
Sprite coordinates for skater 0 (X = 0): continues at $117F with the fields at $46-$55.

Convert object X's ramp coordinates (X = 0: $46-$55; X = $10, the thrown body in a bail: $56-$65) into sprite coordinates: ($B7 - x) and (y - 7) are scaled by the 8.8 factor $51/$52+X with multiply_8x8; sprite X goes to $49/$4A+X (minus $0B on the left half, mirrored as $163 - x when $48 bit 7 is set) and sprite Y to $4B+X (less $0A).

Set $67/$68/$69, from which $0C29 places sprite 7 (sprite 4's image, colour entry 7 of $2E63, which both colour sets make 0): sprite X = $49/$4A; sprite Y = $4B, or while the skater is above the coping ($47 < $96) the sprite Y of the coping itself (y $96 put through the same scaling).
No caller found (same scan as $1124): shift A's high nibble down and draw it through draw_digit at $1223.

Draw A's low nibble as one glyph at $14/$15 from the digit glyph codes at $2CEF (0-9, A-F), masked with $3F. A zero while $38 is zero draws a space ($20) instead (leading-zero blanking); a nonzero digit sets $38.

Load file $0F through the resident loader with X/Y = $00/$68 (JMP $F230). copy_inverted_glyph and $1599 read their glyphs from $6800, so X/Y is consistent with a load address. Called once at the event start ($088A).

Set the glyph column from A ($1294), take the caller's return address as a pointer, draw the zero-terminated bytes after the JSR (each AND $3F, inverted, through $1258) and return to the byte after the terminator. Only caller $099E; its text is $09A1-$09C9.
Draw the zero-terminated string at ($12) with copy_inverted_glyph, each byte AND $3F, leaving $12/$13 on the terminator. Called by $1242 and $09D9.
Copy glyph A (eight bytes at $6800 + A*8) inverted (EOR $FF) to the destination $14/$15, then advance $14/$15 by eight to the next character cell.
Set the glyph destination $14/$15 to $4000 + A*8: cell A of the first bitmap row, where the header line with PASS and HEIGHT is drawn.

Map object X's 16-bit path position $54/$55+X to ramp coordinates $46/$47+X through the 274 (x, y) pairs at $2ACB-$2CEE: s < $111 indexes directly (left half), s >= $111 as $222 - s (right half), and the half is rotated into bit 7 of $48+X. Negative s or s > $222 returns the first pair's x with y moved by the overshoot, carry set; otherwise carry clear, $12/$13 left on the pair.
Zero $12-$72, the event's zero-page variables. Called at the event start ($08B3).

Build the quarter-square tables for multiply_8x8: floor(n*n/4) for n = 0-511, low bytes at $0400-$05FF, high bytes at $0600-$07FF (checked against the snapshot for all 512). Called at the event start ($08B6).

Fill reverse_bits_table at $2E7B (each byte with its eight bits reversed) and reverse_pixel_pairs_table at $2F7B (its four two-bit pixels reversed), used to mirror hires and multicolour sprite rows. Called at the event start ($08B9).

Unsigned 8 x 8 multiply: returns A*Y with the low byte in A and the high byte in Y, as q(A+Y) - q(|A-Y|) with q from the tables at $0400-$07FF (checked for all 65,536 operand pairs). Writes A into the operands at $137E/$1385 so that the indexed loads read q(A+Y). Uses X.
Low byte of the q(A+Y) low-table load's base, written with A by multiply_8x8 at $136A; the snapshot holds $8F, the last A.
Low byte of the q(A+Y) high-table load's base ($06xx), written with A at $136D.

Build one 64-byte sprite block mirrored left to right for hires data: read the descriptor ($1419), clear the bytes after its last index $18, then for each three-byte row swap the outer bytes and reverse the bits of all three (reverse_bits_table); advance to the next descriptor and block ($1432).
Like mirror_hires_sprite_block, but reverses the two-bit pixels of each byte (reverse_pixel_pairs_table at $2F7B), mirroring multicolour sprite data.
Build one 64-byte sprite block unmirrored: clear the bytes after the descriptor's last index $18 and copy bytes $18 down to 0 from the source, then advance ($1432).

Read the six-byte sprite descriptor at ($29): bytes 0-1 plus the base at $2E61/$2E62 ($8284) give the source in $12/$13, byte 2 the index of its last byte in $18. Bytes 3 and 4 are the X and Y offsets that $0C4C adds.
Advance the descriptor pointer $29/$2A by six and the output pointer $14/$15 by 64, to the next sprite block.
Called only from $1743 and $1756, which have no callers themselves: decrease the scale $51/$52 by one unless it is below $00C0.
Called only from $1743 and $1756: increase the scale $51/$52 by one while it is below $0100.

Physics step for object X: look up the ramp pair ($12A0). On the table the acceleration $18 is the y of the pair 16 places on minus this pair's y (the slope), skipped for pairs from $2CCF on; off the table (carry) it is $10, gravity. Velocity $4D/$4E+X gains $18 on the left half and loses it on the right; the 24-bit path position $53-$55+X then gains the sign-extended velocity.
Ballistic step for object 1, the body thrown in a bail (phase $06 at $0E91): add 1 to x $56, add the vertical velocity $5D/$5E to $3B/$57 (fraction, y), then add $10 to the velocity.

Swap the sprite buffers ($22 toggles between pointers $B0 and $B8, data at $6C00/$6E00) and build five sprite blocks from pose $4F's 30-byte record ($7000 + pose*30, $095D): copies when $48 bit 7 is set, mirrored (hires 1, 4, 5; multicolour 2, 3) when clear. While $25 is negative (bail) blocks 1-4 come from object 1's pose $5F (facing $58) and block 5 from pose $4F's fifth descriptor. Called from $0CF6.

No caller found (same scan as $1124): would draw the height $2B like draw_height_digits (two feet glyphs, two inch glyphs) but into sprite data at $6D40 (pointer $B5) through $1599, at byte offsets $12, $13, $52 and $53.
Copy glyph A's eight bytes ($6800 + A*8, for A below $40) into one byte column of sprite data at $6D40 + Y, three bytes apart. Only called from $155C.
Pseudo-random byte: step the generator state $2E5F/$2E60 (a shift with feedback from $2E5F) and return ($2E5F + $2E60) XOR the frame counter $2C in A.
Random number from 0 to A-1: multiply a random_byte by A (multiply_8x8) and return the high byte in A and Y.
Increment the 16-bit frame counter $2C/$2D; called once a frame from the raster handler at $0B2E.

Set the phase $2E to A, do that phase's setup, and zero the tick counters $31/$32. $00: scale $51/$52 = $00F8, fractions $4C/$53 and height $2B cleared, HEIGHT and PASS redrawn. $02: clear $36, $26, $33, $27, $28 (and lock controls on the left half with six or more passes). $08: clear $27. $06: bail set-up at $163C. $10: place_skater_on_platform. Other values: counters only.

Phase $06 set-up: clear height $2B and the lock $43; start object 1 (the body) at the skater's x with y $96, its facing, scale and platform path position; $3C = $F8, velocity $5D/$5E = 0, zoom step $60 = $7A, or -$7A when the scale is $E0 or more; $27 = 1 when the speed $4D/$4E is $0348 or more either way, choosing sound $16 or $09 from $2DB7 and the fall tables at $2A6F/$2A71.

Sound for this transition by speed: X ($27, used here as a temporary) is 1 when the speed word $4D/$4E is $0348 or more either way ($1684-$169A), else 0; queue sound highjump_transition_sound_ids[X] ($2DB7): 22 when slower, 9 when faster.
Friction for skater 0 (X = 0): continues at $16C3.
No caller found (same scan as $1124): friction for object 1, X = $10, through $16C3.
Take 1/256 of object X's 24-bit velocity $4E:$4D:$4C off it (subtract the value shifted right eight bits, sign-extended). Phases $02, $06 and $08 call it once a frame; $18B1 twice.

Pumping, called by phase $02 while the skater is low in the ramp ($23 >= $B0): any newly pressed joystick direction ($30 low nibble not $0F), or every frame while the attempt is over ($43 set, so no input is needed), restarts a boost with $36 = 10 minus the whole part of the speed. Each frame $36 counts down and $2DBD[$36] (6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1) is added to the speed $4D/$4E in the direction of travel.

Once per stretch, from phase $02: after entering it ($26 = 0) queue sound $0F when the skater reaches the lower ramp ($23 >= $E0); after crossing the centre ($26 = 1, set at $0CCC) queue sound $10 when it rises above $F0. Then $26 = $FF.
No caller found (same scan as $1124): joystick up ($2F bit 0 low) steps the scale $51/$52 down ($1449), down (bit 1) steps it up ($145E).
No caller found: steps the scale with up/down like $1743 and, on the left half, snaps it to $D8 (up) or $E8 (down) when it lands in $D9-$E6 ($1818); going up it also holds it at $C3 or more.

Called by phase $02 ($0E3E) when it picks a pose while $37 is negative ($0CC8 sets $37 = $FF at every centre crossing): $37 = 1, ending the run at the next coping (phase $0E, height capped), when the controls are locked ($43) or the skater is on the left half with five or more passes; otherwise $37 = 0 and the height $2B is cleared for the new pass. Returns $37 in A.

Draw the HEIGHT value from $2B at header cell $21: feet ($2B / 8) as two glyphs from $2DC7, glyph $27 ('), inches for $2B AND 7 as two glyphs from $2DF1, glyph $22 ("). One unit of $2B is an eighth of a foot.
Draw the pass count $3A as one digit at header cell $16 through draw_digit, with leading-zero blanking off ($38 = $FF).
No caller found (same scan as $1124): add the signed byte A to the 24-bit scale $50-$52 (values $80-$FF borrow one from $51/$52 first).
Called only from $1756: carry set when the skater is on the left half ($48 bit 7 clear) and the scale $51/$52 is $D9-$E6.
Carry set when the scale $51/$52 is below $00BF or $0101 and over; clear for $BF-$100. Used by phase $06 ($0E61) and $19F8.
Add A to the sprite descriptor pointer $29/$2A: 6 skips one descriptor, $18 four. Called by $0BE8, $0C04 and $154D.
Hold the scale $51/$52 within $00A8-$0108. Called every frame from the raster band at $0CBD.
Phase $06: while the step $60 is nonzero, add it (signed) to the 24-bit scale $50-$52 and move it two closer to zero, so the scale eases by a shrinking amount. bail_setup sets $60 to $7A or $86.

Phase $06 alternative when the scale is outside $BF-$100 ($1834); not executed in the simulated runs. While scale < $E0 add $3C to $3D (a carry moves x $46 right and $51 down) and cut $3C by 4; pose $4F = 0; gravity $10 into $4D/$4E above the floor; y $47 += velocity, held at $F0 with the velocity halved and reversed; friction twice; display update.
Carry set when the scale $51/$52 is $00E0 or more. Called by bail_setup and $18B1.
Starting push velocity in X (low) and Y (high): $0080 on the left half, $FF80 on the right ($48 bit 7), half a path unit a frame towards the centre. Callers store it in $4D/$4E.

Flip two-frame animated cell A (0-$44) of the picture: bitmap address $4000 + the word cell_bitmap_offsets[A]; bit 7 of $1CA5[2A] toggles to pick frame 2A or 2A+1; that frame's screen byte ($1C1B) goes to $6400 + offset/8, its colour ($1CA5) to $D800 + offset/8, and its eight bitmap bytes from $1D2F + frame*8.
Animate cells A and A+1 with animate_cell.

From the raster handler ($0B51), once a frame: when a random byte AND 7 is zero, animate a random pair among cells 0-7 (A = 0, 2, 4 or 6) and return carry set; otherwise carry clear, and the caller runs height_cell_animation twice.

If a random byte is not above $3F, animate one random cell from 8 to $44. $3F is set to half the height $2B at each turnaround ($1AD0) and counted down every fourth frame by the raster handler once $40 has run out, so higher passes animate more cells for longer. Also called up to ten times a frame from $0D1B.

Event start (from $08CB): clear the pass count $3A, queue sound 1 unless sound is off ($FE10), copy one of two eight-byte sprite colour sets, $2D7F or $2D87 chosen at random, to $2E63, and enter phase $00.
Every frame from the raster band ($0D0D): enable sprite 7 ($66 = $80, ORed into $D015 at $0B5D) when the scale is within $BF-$100, else $66 = 0; then set_sprite7_position.

Every frame from the raster handler ($0B36): compare keyboard row 7 ($DC01, with $DC00 = $7F) with the previous value $6D; a newly pressed RUN/STOP (bit 7) sets $FE12 = $FF and ends the event through $1A49, from inside the interrupt.
Every frame from the raster handler ($0B39): a newly pressed C= key (row 7 bit 5, previous value $6E) flips the sound-off flag $FE10 and copies it to $6F; turning sound back on queues sound 1.

End of the event (phase $10 with fire, or RUN/STOP): leave the height for the resident code, raw $2B in $FE05, feet as BCD in $FE04 and inches as BCD in $FE03 (low nibbles of the glyph codes from $2DC7/$2DF1); turn all sprites off ($D015 = 0), reset the sound system ($22B7) and JMP $FE06.
Append sound ID A to the 16-entry ring $2E6B at write index $70, with no overflow check. The main loop drains it ($1AA5, $22F5).
Return the next sound ID from the ring $2E6B and advance the read index $71; the main loop calls it while $71 differs from $70.
Every frame from the raster band ($0CBA): height = $96 - $23 (pixels above the coping) + the bonus $44, counted as 0 when $96 or more; if not below $2B it becomes $2B. Clears $44 and redraws HEIGHT.

When the sign of velocity $4E differs from the last one ($42): queue sound $14, set the countdowns $40 = $2B and $3F = $2B/2, and on the right half ($48 bit 7) add a pass to $3A, locking the controls ($43 = $FF) at five; redraw PASS. Called by phases $04, $08, $0A.

Event start ($08BC): write $07 into ten screen-matrix bytes from $604C, 40 apart, clear the low two bits of the eight bytes from $4258 and copy eight bytes from $2E07 + 8k to $4260 + $140k, k = 0-9: a strip in cell column 36, rows 1-10 of the bitmap.

Unpack run-length data from ($12) to ($14) until $12/$13 reaches the end address in $16/$17: a control byte $00-$7F copies the next n+1 bytes; $80-$FF repeats the next byte n-$7F times. Called at $090F.

Animated-cell table read by animate_cell ($192E): one little-endian word per cell number 0-$44, the cell offset into the bitmap (bitmap at $4000 + word; screen and colour bytes at word/8). Entry 0 is $0408. The 69 words run $1B91-$1C1A, past this range; $1BFF is the low byte of entry 55, whose high byte is $1C00.

High byte of cell_bitmap_offsets entry 0; animate_cell reads the high bytes as $1B92,X and the low bytes as $1B91,X with X = 2 x cell. Entries 0-7 are the cells random_pair_animation flips, 8-$44 those height_cell_animation flips.
cell_bitmap_offsets from entry 32 (cell $20, offset $0A70) on, continued past $1BFF; still the table read by animate_cell.
Low byte ($E8) of cell_bitmap_offsets entry 55, offset $0BE8; its high byte $0B is at $1C00, outside this range.
High byte ($0B) of entry 55 of the animated-cell offset table that starts at $1B91 (bitmap offset $0BD8, the crowd cell at text row 9, column 19); the table is read by $192E.

Entries 56-68 of the animated-cell offset table from $1B91: bitmap offsets ($0BE0-$0D50) of the last crowd cells, rows 9-10. $192E derives the bitmap address ($4000+offset), the screen byte ($6400+offset/8) and the colour-RAM byte from each.

Screen-matrix byte (multicolour bitmap colours %01 high nibble, %10 low nibble) for each animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell (frame 0, frame 1): this label covers cells 0-31. $192E writes the chosen frame's byte to $6400 + cell offset/8. Cells 0-7 are the four flags of text row 3, cells 8-68 the crowd in rows 7-10.
Screen-matrix colour bytes, frame 0 then frame 1, for animated cells 32-63 (crowd, text rows 8-9); continues anim_cell_screen_colours.
Screen-matrix colour bytes for the last animated cells 64-68 (crowd, rows 9-10), frame 0 then frame 1; ends at $1CA4.

Colour-RAM byte (colour of %11 pixels, low nibble) per animated cell and frame, two bytes per cell, cells 0-31 here. Bit 7 of each cell's first byte is the frame flag: $192E flips it at $195A and shows frame 1 when it ends up set, so the table is rewritten during play.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags (bit 7 of the first byte) for animated cells 32-63; continues anim_cell_colour_ram.
Colour-RAM bytes and frame flags for animated cells 64-68; ends at $1D2E.

Bitmap pixels of the animated background cells, 8 bytes per frame, frame 0 then frame 1 of each cell (entry = cell*2 + frame), copied to the bitmap at $4000 + cell offset by $1986-$198D. This label: cells 0-3 (the two left flags on row 3).
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 4-7 (flags), at $1D6F-$1DAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 8-11 (crowd), at $1DAF-$1DEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 12-15 (crowd), at $1DEF-$1E2E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 16-19 (crowd), at $1E2F-$1E6E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 20-23 (crowd), at $1E6F-$1EAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 24-27 (crowd), at $1EAF-$1EEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 28-31 (crowd), at $1EEF-$1F2E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 32-35 (crowd), at $1F2F-$1F6E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 36-39 (crowd), at $1F6F-$1FAE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 40-43 (crowd), at $1FAF-$1FEE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 44-47 (crowd), at $1FEF-$202E.
Not code: bitmap bytes of animated cell 47, frame 0. The automatic symbol here comes from the inline text after $099E ($09A1-$09C9) being decoded as code, where $20 $20 reads as JSR $2020.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 48-51 (crowd), at $202F-$206E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 52-55 (crowd), at $206F-$20AE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 56-59 (crowd), at $20AF-$20EE.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 60-63 (crowd), at $20EF-$212E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 64-67 (crowd), at $212F-$216E.
Animated-cell bitmaps (8 bytes per frame, two frames per cell), cells 68-68 (crowd), at $216F-$217E.

156 bytes after the last animated-cell bitmap, up to the sound driver's variables. No instruction found that addresses them (opcode scan, cross-references) and none was read or written in simulated play; their pattern resembles the uninitialised call-stack bytes at $2287. Purpose unknown; probably file slack.

Number of sound IDs waiting in pending_sound_ids ($2277), 0-16. queue_sound_id ($22F5) appends while it is below $10 (a 17th request is dropped); update_sid_voices ($232C) drains it to zero each tick. Cleared with the rest of $221B-$2286 by init_sound_driver.

Lowest priority among the three slots (the one a new sound must equal or beat). Recomputed at $29BC-$29D5 after each start; set to 0 when a slot finishes ($2921), so the next request always wins that free slot.
Slot offset (0, 2 or 4) of the slot holding sound_weakest_priority: where start_sound_on_weakest_slot ($2981) puts the next accepted sound. Set at $29D8 and, when a slot ends, at $2924.
The primary-script command byte being executed, saved by dispatch_sound_opcode ($2396). Handlers test its bit 7 (BIT $221E) for the operand mode and op 7 re-reads its high nibble.
Low byte of the left-hand value for sound op 6 (compare): the slot's frequency, pulse width, sustain level, loop counter or a byte read from memory; $2220 holds the high byte for 16-bit compares.
High byte of the 16-bit left-hand compare value (frequency or pulse width) for sound op 6, compared first at $26AD.
Low byte (or only byte) of the right-hand operand of sound op 6, fetched by $26C9/$26DC from the script or through an address.
High byte of the right-hand operand for 16-bit compares in sound op 6 (set by $26DC).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency low byte, at $2223/$2225/$2227 for slot offsets 0/2/4 (voices 3/2/1). Written with every frequency change and read back by op 4 (add) and op 6 (compare).
Per-slot shadow of the SID frequency high byte, at $2224/$2226/$2228 for slot offsets 0/2/4; paired with slot_freq_lo.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width low byte, at $2229/$222B/$222D for slot offsets 0/2/4; set by op 1 and note command $AD, added to by op 4, compared by op 6.
Per-slot shadow of the SID pulse-width high nibble, at $222A/$222C/$222E for slot offsets 0/2/4.
Low byte of slot 0's call-stack base address (init_sound_driver stores $2287); the three slots' base pointers are words at $222F, $2231, $2233, read as $222F,x at $2608 and $2928.
High byte of slot 0's call-stack base ($22), read as $2230,x with the low byte at $222F,x.
Low byte of slot 2's (SID voice 2's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $97, so slot 2 nests at $2297.
High byte of slot 2's call-stack base ($22).
Low byte of slot 4's (SID voice 1's) call-stack base: init_sound_driver stores $A7, so slot 4 nests at $22A7.
High byte of slot 4's call-stack base ($22).

Four note durations per slot, $2235-$2238 (slot 0), $2239-$223C (slot 2), $223D-$2240 (slot 4), indexed by slot*2 + bits 7-6 of a note byte. The chosen value goes to the slot's wait timer ($224D,x). Loaded by op $97 and note command $5D.

Four gate lengths per slot, $2241-$2244, $2245-$2248, $2249-$224C, chosen like slot_note_durations. Non-zero: the note sets the gate bit and the gate timer ($224E,x); zero: the note changes pitch without re-gating. Loaded by op $A7 and note command $6D.

Per-slot wait timer at $224D/$224F/$2251 (slot offsets 0/2/4): while non-zero update_sid_voices decrements it instead of reading the script; a value N set in one tick makes the slot read again N+1 ticks later (checked against SID writes in the simulator). Set by op 8, notes and note commands.

Per-slot gate timer at $224E/$2250/$2252: when flag bit 5 is set it counts down each tick and, G+1 ticks after a value G was set, clears the gate bit (bit 0) of the voice's control register ($235D), starting the release. The shadow $225A,x keeps the gate bit.
Sound ID playing in each slot, at $2253/$2255/$2257; 0 after the slot ends. stop_sound ($2303) searches it.
Per-slot flags at $2254/$2256/$2258: 0 idle; bit 6 active (set to $40 at start); bit 5 gate timer running; bit 4 inside a script call (call stack non-empty); bit 7 paused (skipped by the updater).
Per-slot sustain level counter (low nibble used) at $2259/$225B/$225D: op $24 adds to it and writes it as the high nibble of the SID sustain/release register; op $26 compares it.
Per-slot shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits and gate) at $225A/$225C/$225E; the gate timer clears bit 0 from it, notes set bit 0.
Per-slot loop counter at $225F/$2261/$2263: set by op $31, added to by op $34, compared by op $36, and decremented by the loop op $15 (jump while non-zero).

Priority of the sound in slot 0 (SID voice 3); the slots' priorities are at $2260/$2262/$2264. Set from sound_priorities ($30AF) on start, cleared at end; compared at $29BC-$29D5 to find the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 2 (SID voice 2), read directly at $29C1/$29C8 when finding the weakest slot.
Priority of the sound in slot 4 (SID voice 1), read directly at $29BE when finding the weakest slot (slot 4 is the first candidate).
Per-slot shadow of the SID attack/decay register at $2265/$2267/$2269; set by op $41 and note command $8D.
Per-slot shadow of the SID sustain/release register at $2266/$2268/$226A; op $24 rewrites its high nibble from slot_sustain_level.

Bytes used on each slot's call stack at $226B/$226D/$226F (two per nested call); a call pushes the return pointer at stack base + depth, a return pops it. Not range-checked: more than 8 nested calls would run into the next slot's stack.
Result of the slot's last op 6 compare at $226C/$226E/$2270, as the processor's C and Z bits: 0 less, 1 greater, 3 equal. Tested by the conditional jumps of op 5 against $2635/$263B.

Per-slot octave shift at $2271/$2273/$2275: the number of right shifts applied to note frequencies before the note's own octave bits are added (note_frequency, $28E3). Set by op $B7 and note command $4D.
Sixteen-byte queue of requested sound IDs: queue_sound_id ($22F5) appends while sound_pending_count is below $10; update_sid_voices starts them newest first and empties the queue each tick.

Three 16-byte call stacks for nested sound scripts, $2287 (slot 0), $2297 (slot 2), $22A7 (slot 4), addressed through slot_stack_ptr_lo/hi. Each call pushes a two-byte return address. Not cleared by init: the bytes here are whatever the file carried; 8 levels per slot.

Sound driver reset: zero the script pointers $02-$07 and all driver state $221B-$2286, silence the three SID control registers, set volume $0F with no filter ($D418), and point the slots' call stacks at $2287/$2297/$22A7. Called at $08C8, from the main loop when $6F is set ($08D3), and at $1A90.

Request sound ID A: append it to pending_sound_ids unless 16 are already waiting (then the request is silently dropped). Called from the main loop ($08E3, IDs from the game's own request ring at $1AA5) and by sound op 2. Clobbers X.

Stop sound ID A wherever it plays: search slot_sound_id for slots 4, 2, 0 and, if found, silence that slot through $2910 with interrupts disabled. No caller in High Jump (no reference found by opcode scan); part of the shared driver.
Found: Y = the slot's SID register offset; silence the slot with IRQs masked.
Set slot A (0-2, doubled to the slot offset) to flags $80 so update_sid_voices skips it. It replaces all flags rather than setting bit 7. No caller in High Jump.
Clear bit 7 of slot A's flags. After pause_sound_slot the flags are $80, so this leaves 0 (idle) and the slot does not resume. No caller in High Jump.

One sound tick (run by the main loop once per raster frame counted in $72): start every queued ID (start_sound_on_weakest_slot), then for slots 4, 2, 0 (SID voices 1, 2, 3): skip if idle or paused; run the gate timer; if the wait timer is zero, execute script commands until a $00 byte (end of tick) or the slot ends.
Read the next byte of slot X's primary script through ($02,X) and advance the pointer; the Z flag reflects the byte (a $00 byte ends the tick at $237A).

Execute primary command A: save it in sound_command_byte, push the handler for its low nibble from $23AE/$23BE (RTS trick), and enter it with A = high nibble. Bit 7 of the command is the operand-mode flag; bits 6-4 select the sub-operation.

High bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one, indexed by the low nibble of the command: 0 end/return ($2909), 1 set register ($23CE), 2 queue sound ($2492), 3 poke/wait ($24A1), 4 add ($250C), 5 jump/loop/call ($259B), 6 compare ($2641), 7 note stream ($26FA), 8 wait ($28F1), 9 end, A call 6502 code ($2951), B-F end.
Low bytes of the 16 primary sound-op handlers minus one (paired with $23AE); RTS lands one byte higher, on the handler.

Op $x1, set a voice register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency (2 bytes lo,hi), 1-2 pulse width (2), 3 loop counter (1), 4 attack/decay (1), 5 sustain/release (1), 6-7 control/waveform (1). Bit 7 clear: the value follows in the script; bit 7 set: a 2-byte address follows and the value is read from there. Writes the SID and the slot shadow.
Op $02: the next script byte is a sound ID to request through queue_sound_id (started at the next tick, by priority); X and Y preserved.

Op 3 with an address operand (2 bytes). Sub-op 1 ($13/$93), wait-until: compare memory at the address with a value (bit 7 set: a literal byte; clear: a byte read through a second address); if unequal, back the script up 4 bytes and end this slot's tick, so it retries next tick. Other sub-ops ($03/$83), poke: store a value there (bit 7 clear: literal; set: read through a second address).

Unequal: rewind the script by 4 (right for the literal form $93 aa aa vv; the address form is 5 bytes long, so it would resume on its second byte), drop the dispatcher's return and go to the next slot.

Op 4, add to a register, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency += 2-byte value (bit 7 set: value read through an address), 1 pulse width += 2 bytes, 2 sustain level += byte, rewrite sustain/release and set the gate bit (re-trigger), 3+ loop counter += byte. Writes the SID and the shadows; 16-bit adds wrap.

Op 5, script flow. Bit 7 clear: $05 jump to a 2-byte address; $15 decrement the loop counter, jump while non-zero, else skip the address; $25 call (push the return pointer on the slot's stack, set flag bit 4); $35 replace this slot's sound with the ID in the next byte; others end. Bit 7 set: conditional jump on the last compare, $85 equal, $95 less, $A5 not equal, $B5 greater, $C5 less or equal, $D5 greater or equal; $E5/$F5 end.
First accepted compare result for the conditional jumps $85-$D5 (index = bits 6-4): 3,0,1,1,0,1. A jump is taken when slot_compare_result equals this byte or the one at $263B.
Second accepted compare result for the conditional jumps (same index): 3,0,0,1,3,3. With $2635 this gives equal, less, not equal (1 or 0), greater, less-or-equal (0 or 3), greater-or-equal (1 or 3).

Op 6, compare and keep the result in slot_compare_result, sub-op = bits 6-4: 0 frequency vs 2-byte operand, 1 pulse width vs 2 bytes, 2 sustain level vs byte, 3 loop counter vs byte, 7 the byte at a 2-byte address vs byte; others end the script. Bit 7 set: the operand is read through an address instead.
Bytes 2C A9 01: BIT $01A9 hides LDA #$01 at $26C3, the entry for 'greater' (result 1); entered at $26C2 it gives 0, 'less'.
Fetch op 6's one-byte right operand into sound_compare_right: the next script byte, or (command bit 7 set) the byte read through a 2-byte address.
Fetch op 6's two-byte right operand into sound_compare_right/_hi: two script bytes, or (command bit 7 set) the word read through a 2-byte address.

Op 7. Bit 7 clear ($07): play the next event of the slot's note stream at ($08,X): low nibble 0-C a note (frequency table index, 0 silent), bits 5-4 extra octave shift, bits 7-6 pick duration and gate length; $xD a note command (handler $27ED by high nibble, next byte its argument); $0E call a primary-script subroutine at the next 2 bytes; else end. Bit 7 set: $87 set the stream pointer, $97 four durations, $A7 four gate lengths, $B7 octave shift.
Read the next byte of slot X's note stream through ($08,X) and advance that pointer.

Low bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, indexed by the high nibble of a $xD stream byte: 0 note+duration, 1 frequency+duration, 2 note+duration+gate, 3 frequency+duration+gate, 4 octave shift, 5 durations, 6 gate lengths, 7 control, 8 attack/decay, 9 sustain/release, A pulse width. $BD-$FD index past the table (no check).
High bytes of the 11 note-stream command handlers, paired with note_command_handlers_lo; read at $2757 and jumped to through $0E/$0F.
Note command $0D: the argument is a note byte (low nibble note, bits 5-4 octave); the next stream byte is a literal duration for the wait timer. Sets the frequency without touching the gate.
Note command $1D: the argument and the next byte are a literal SID frequency (low, high); the next byte is the duration. No gate change.
Note command $2D: note byte argument, then a literal duration and gate length; starts the gate timer (flag bit 5) but does not set the gate bit itself.
Note command $3D: literal frequency (argument = low, next = high), then duration and gate length; starts the gate timer without setting the gate bit.
Note command $4D: the argument becomes the slot's octave shift ($2271,x); then the next stream event is played in the same tick.
Note command $5D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four note durations ($2235); then the next event is played.
Note command $6D: the argument and the next three stream bytes replace the slot's four gate lengths ($2241); then the next event is played.
Note command $7D: write the argument to the voice's SID control register (waveform, gate) and its shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $8D: write the argument to the voice's attack/decay register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $9D: write the argument to the voice's sustain/release register and shadow, then play the next event.
Note command $AD: the argument and the next stream byte are the pulse width (low, high), written to the SID and shadows; then the next event is played.

Note number A (0-15) to frequency in $0E/$0F: read the top-octave value from note_freq_lo/hi and shift it right by (bits 5-4 of the note byte in $11) + the slot's octave shift. Used by notes and note commands $0D/$2D.

Op 8: the next byte is a wait. $08 N: set the slot's wait timer, so the script resumes N+1 ticks later (once a $00 has ended this tick). $88 G: set the gate timer instead and flag bit 5, so the gate is released G+1 ticks later while the script runs on.
Op 0/9/B-F (and every invalid sub-op): if the slot is inside a call (flag bit 4), pop the return pointer from its call stack and continue there; otherwise fall into silence_sound_slot.

End slot X: clear the voice's control register (gate off, no waveform), the slot's ID, flags, stack depth and priority, and make it the weakest slot (priority 0) for the next request. Y = the voice's SID register offset. Also called from stop_sound.
Op $0A: call the 6502 routine at the 2-byte address that follows, preserving X and Y. Sound 1 (music) uses it to call $3517, game code that picks the next phrase.
JMP ($000E): the indirect call made by sound_opA_call_code; returns to $2962 when the called routine executes RTS.

Read a 2-byte address from slot X's script and return the byte there in A and the following byte in $11 (a little-endian word), with Y restored to the voice's SID register offset. The operand form used when a command's bit 7 selects it.

Start sound ID A if its priority (sound_priorities, $30AF) is at least sound_weakest_priority: replace the sound in slot sound_weakest_slot. Equal priority wins, so a new sound replaces an old one of the same rank.

Start sound ID Y with priority A on slot X: set the slot's priority and ID, its script pointer from sound_script_addresses ($307B/$3095), clear its timers and stack, set flags $40, zero the voice's seven SID registers, then find the new weakest slot (slot 4 first, then 2, then 0) for sound_weakest_priority/slot. Also used by op $35.

SID register offset of each sound slot, read at even X only: $29DC (slot 0) $0E = voice 3, $29DE (slot 2) $07 = voice 2, $29E0 (slot 4) $00 = voice 1. The odd bytes $29DD/$29DF are never read as offsets.

Low bytes of the note frequency table, 16 entries indexed by the note's low nibble: 0 silence ($0000), 1-12 the twelve semitones A, A#, B, C ... G# of the top octave ($70C7 ... $D4E6), 13-15 zero. In NTSC SID units entry 1 is 1760 Hz (A6); on a PAL machine it plays about 0.65 semitone flat.

High bytes of the note frequency table ($00,$70,$77,$7E,$86,$8E,$96,$9F,$A8,$B3,$BD,$C8,$D4,0,0,0); each step is a factor of about 1.0595, one semitone. note_frequency shifts the value right once per octave down.

Two raster-band handler addresses, indexed by band number $1E: band 0 $0B21 (line $F9: multicolour off and $D011 = $33, so the top text row, the status line, starts hires; frame counter $72; sprites; per-frame checks and background animation), band 1 $0CA3 (line $37: waits for line $3A, multicolour on, $D011 = $3B, then the game update). The IRQ at $0AF0 patches its JSR at $0B0B with the chosen one.
High byte of each raster-band handler address (table raster_handler_addresses + 1), read at $0B05 to patch the JSR's high operand.

Raster line at which each band's interrupt fires, indexed by band: band 0 $F9 (bottom border), band 1 $37 (top of the display window). Read at $0A2F for the first interrupt and at $0B15 for each next one.
Next band after each band (band 0 -> 1, band 1 -> 0), read at $0B10: the two interrupts alternate, one pair per frame.

Four pose numbers ($08,$08,$30,$18) for $4F, indexed by $37 (or by s_1798's result when $37 is negative), used when the $2A17 band entry is $FF and the skater faces right ($24 positive): phase 2 at $0E42; phase 6 uses entry 0 at $0E86. Entries 0-2 read in simulated play.
Four pose numbers ($10,$10,$35,$20) for $4F, the left-facing ($24 negative) counterpart of pose_by_37_right, read at $0E49. Entries 0-1 read in simulated play.
Phase to enter when phase 2 sees $23 below $96, indexed by $37: 0 -> $04, 1 -> $0E (read at $0E57, passed to set_highjump_phase).

Four flags indexed by $37 at $1168: non-zero clamps the coordinate $23 to at least $96. Values 0,1,1,0. Simulated play read entries 0-2 and also $2B12, i.e. $37 = $FF: the index is not checked and that read lands in ramp_path.

Five 3-byte entries: upper bound of the coordinate $23, pose for facing right, pose for facing left ($BA,$FF,$FF / $D6,3,7 / $E3,2,6 / $EC,1,5 / $FF,0,4). Searched upward at $0E28 (phase 2) and $0E7C (phase 6) until $23 is below the bound; a pose of $FF means use pose_by_37_right/left.
The pose columns of pose_bands_by_23 (table + 1), read directly at $0E81 by phase 6, which always takes the facing-right pose; phase 2 reads them through $2A17,y at $0E35.

15 bytes: a second copy of pose_bands_by_23's first four entries followed by $FF,$28,$29. No instruction found that addresses them and none was read in simulated play; the band search could only reach them with $23 = $FF. Purpose unknown.
Ten pose numbers for the skater waiting on the platform, indexed by the step counter $32 (0-9) in phase 0 at $0DB6; entry 0 ($81) is also the pose set at load ($09F7).
Seven pose numbers ($08,$17,$16,$15,$14,$3E,$3F) played through the pointer $1C: phases 8 ($102E, forward) and $0A ($1074, reversed). $0F5B selects this table when the pose was $08.
Seven pose numbers ($10,$11,$12,$13,$14,$3E,$3F), the left-facing counterpart of turn_poses_right, selected at $0F66 when the pose was $10. Not read in the simulated runs.
Five (bound, value) pairs searched at $0EA1 in phase 6: the first bound above $57 gives the value stored in $5F ($A8:$2A, $B8:$2B, $C8:$2C, $DC:$2D, $FF:$2D).
The value column of value_bands_by_57 (table + 1), read at $0EA6 once the bound search at $0EA1 stops; the value goes to $5F.
Six values ($8C-$91) for $5F, indexed by $32 in phase 6 when X = $27 is 0 (read at $0EDD).
Six values ($FE,$FE,$F8,$F8,$F8,$F8) for $45, indexed by $32 in phase 6 when $27 is 0 (read at $0ED8).
Twelve values ($92-$9D) for $5F, indexed by $32 in phase 6 when $27 is 1 or more (read at $0ED1).
Length of the phase 6 sequence for $27 = 0 (6) and 1 (12), compared with $32 at $0EB6/$0ECB; at the end the phase moves on ($0EEE).
Amount added to $56 on each phase 6 step for $27 = 0 and 1 (both 0 in this load), read at $0EE2.
Seven pose numbers ($69,$6A,$6B,$6C,$6D,$6D,$6D) for phase $0E, indexed by $32 (0-6), facing right; read at $10AD.
Seven pose numbers for phase $0E facing left ($24 negative), indexed by $32; read at $10B4.
Ten pose numbers for phase $10, indexed by $32 (0-9), used when the height $2B is below $50 (read at $1106).
Ten pose numbers for phase $10 when the height $2B is $50-$67 (read at $1100).
Ten pose numbers for phase $10 when the height $2B is $68 or more (read at $10FA).
Twelve pose numbers for phase $0C (platform idle animation), indexed by $32, when the random choice $33 is 0 (read at $0DEE).
Twelve pose numbers for phase $0C when $33 is 1 (read at $0DF5).
Length of the phase $0C pose run for $33 = 0 and 1 (12 each), compared with $32 at $0DDC; at the end the phase returns to 0.
Nine little-endian code pointers, selected by even state value $2E at $0D3F and patched into the call at $0D4E. Entries cover states $00,$02,$04,$06,$08,$0A,$0C,$0E,$10.
High byte of each phase handler address (highjump_phase_handlers + 1), read at $0D47 to patch the high operand of the JMP at $0D4D.

273 two-byte entries ($2ACB-$2CEE), indexed by the skater's position $54/$55 (0-$110; positions $111-$222 read it mirrored, index $222 - position) at lookup_skater_position ($12A0): byte 0 goes to $46,x, byte 1 to $47,x. Byte 0 stays $2A for entries 0-108 then rises to $B5; byte 1 rises one per entry from $40 and levels at $F0: a quarter-pipe profile (an inference). On the platform, entry $56 = ($2A,$96), as in the snapshot's $46/$47.
Byte 1 of ramp_path's first entry ($40); read directly with $2ACB at $12EC/$12FB when the position is clamped to an end. Entries 0-31 of ramp_path, $2ACB-$2B0A.
ramp_path bytes $2B0C-$2B4B (byte 1 of entry 32 to byte 0 of entry 64): byte 0 still $2A, byte 1 $60-$7F.
ramp_path bytes $2B4C-$2B8B (byte 1 of entry 64 to byte 0 of entry 96): byte 0 $2A, byte 1 $80-$9F; entry $56 (86), the platform position, is here.
ramp_path bytes $2B8C-$2BCB (byte 1 of entry 96 to byte 0 of entry 128): byte 0 leaves $2A at entry 109 and reaches $30; byte 1 $A0-$BF.
ramp_path from byte 1 of entry 128 (byte 1 $C0-$D9, byte 0 $30-$3F up to entry 154 at $2BFF); the table continues to $2CEE, outside this label.

Second part of the two-byte ramp table ramp_path that starts at $2ACB (entry k at $2ACB+2k): $2C00 is the second byte of entry 154, then entries 155-273 run to $2CEE. In this part the first byte rises from $3F to $B6; the second rises by one per entry from $DA and stays at $F0 from entry 209 on. Read through read_ptr12_byte ($0AD1) by lookup_skater_position ($12A0) into $46,X/$47,X, and at $1481/$1485 in integrate_object_motion, which subtracts the second byte of an entry from the one 16 entries later.
Sixteen digit characters 0-9 and A-F (ASCII $30-$39, $41-$46). $1231 indexes it with a value's low nibble, keeps the low six bits and passes the glyph to copy_inverted_glyph ($126D).

64-byte sprite image copied by $0A01 to $6D40, sprite block $B5, which $0B90 puts in sprite 5's pointer at $67FD. Each 3-byte row starts with a tick: $EA on most rows, $FA every fourth and $FE every eighth, $FF on the first: a scale drawn as a sprite.
Second 64-byte scale sprite, copied by $0A07 to $6D80, block $B6, pointed to by sprite 6 at $67FE. Same tick pattern as $2CFF; $2E05/$2E06 place the two sprites 42 lines apart, one above the other.
Eight sprite colours, one per sprite 0-7, copied to sprite_colours ($2E63) by $19DC when random_below ($15DA) called with 2 at $19D3 returns 0: one of two colour sets chosen at random.
Entry for sprite 4 in colour set A: written at load time by $09F1 with the byte at $FE02 in the resident high-RAM area, so its value comes from before High Jump was loaded.
Eight sprite colours, the alternative set, copied to sprite_colours ($2E63) by $19EA when random_below(2) at $19D3 returns 1. Differs from set A in sprites 0, 2 and 3.
Sprite 4 entry of colour set B, patched at load by $09F4 with the same $FE02 byte as $2D83.
Forty screen-RAM bytes copied by $0993 to $6400-$6427, the top row of the bitmap screen: colour pairs $61 and $6E for the 40 cells behind the PASS and HEIGHT header.

Sound IDs. $16A2 plays entry $27: 0 = sound 22 ($342C) when the speed $4D/$4E is within about +/-$0348, 1 = sound 9 ($31D5) when faster. Entries $2DB9-$2DBC (21, 13, 15, 14) are valid sound IDs but no instruction found reads them.

Ten speed increments, indexed by the countdown $36 in pump_speed at $1709/$1718 (added when $4E is positive, subtracted when negative): 1, 2, 3, 4 for counts 0-3, then 6. $16F6 starts the count at 10 minus the size of the speed's high byte, so a pump gives less the faster the skater goes.
Twenty-one two-glyph entries for feet 0 through 20, rendered by draw_height_digits from height byte $2B divided by eight.
Second glyph of each feet pair, read at $17CA and $1A61 with the same index as $2DC7.
Eight two-glyph rounded-inch entries for remainders 0 through 7: 00,02,03,05,06,08,09,11. Live tests gave $2B=$04 -> 0 feet 6 inches and $2B=$08 -> 1 foot 0 inches.
Second glyph of each rounded-inch pair, read at $17E5 and $1A80 with the index used for $2DF1.
Two sprite X low bytes ($40, $40), read at $0C96 into $D000,X for the two scale sprites.
Two X bit-8 values (1, 1), read at $0C9C and shifted into the $D010 byte being built in $1B: both scale sprites sit at X = $140.
Two sprite Y positions ($3C, $66), read at $0C8E into $D001,X: the upper and lower scale sprites, 42 lines apart.

Ten 8-byte bitmap cells (80 bytes) drawn by draw_side_strip ($1AFA, called at $08BC) into the bitmap at $4260 and every $140 below it, a column of ten cells, after clearing the low pixel pair of the cells at $4258; $1AFA also writes colour 7 into ten screen bytes from $604C, $28 apart.
Bit masks $01-$80 for sprites 0-7. $0B9D ANDs each with $45: when the bit is set the sprite takes its colour from $2E63, otherwise it gets 0 (black).
Random number state, low byte: rotated by random_byte ($15C1), which returns ($2E5F + $2E60) XOR $2C. $098B copies it into $2E60 at load.
Random number state, second byte, rotated in by $15CA and added at $15D4.
Low byte of the X register returned by the loader for file $11 at $0951 ($84 in the snapshot); added at $141E to the frame offsets read through ($29).
High byte of the loader's return, from Y at $0954 ($82): with $2E61 gives $8284, the address the next load (file $12, $0959) is given, and the base added at $1426.
Current colours of sprites 0-7, filled from set A ($2D7F) or set B ($2D87) by $19DC/$19EA and written to $D027,X by $0BA2 for each sprite whose bit in $45 is set.

Sixteen-entry ring of sound IDs. queue_event_sound ($1A96) stores at index $70 (wrapping at 16); the main loop at $08DA, when $71 differs from $70, takes the next one at index $71 through dequeue_event_sound ($1AA5) and passes it to queue_sound_id ($22F5).
All 256 entries equal the input byte with its eight individual bits reversed; the graphics builder at $138D applies it while forming a 64-byte block.
All 256 entries equal the input byte with its four two-bit pixel pairs reversed; the graphics builder at $13C5 applies it while forming a 64-byte block.
Twenty-six sound-script addresses in split low/high arrays, indexed by the sound ID at $2994/$2999; the first points to $30CC.
High bytes of the 26 sound-script addresses, read by $2999 into $03,X; the low bytes are at $307B.
Twenty-six one-byte priorities indexed by sound ID; $2982 compares the incoming value against the current voice threshold before allocation.

Sound script for IDs 3, 24 and 25: the single byte $09, an end command, so those IDs start nothing. Sound-script bytecode, run by update_sid_voices ($232C): low nibble = command, high nibble = variant, bit 7 = operand taken from an address; $00 ends the voice's turn for this tick.
Script variable (two bytes; only $30CA is compared): set to $FE by sounds 6, 7 and 8 when they start or finish, set to 1 by sound 0; those three loops end early when they see 1.
Sound 0: poke $30CA = 1, yield, end. Its only effect is to stop the repeating noise of sounds 6, 7 and 8. No High Jump code found queues ID 0.
Sound 5: triangle wave at $6000, AD $80 SR $F9; each tick add $05C0 until $C800, gate off and subtract $0340 to $3200, up again to $E800, down to $2C00, end. No High Jump call found queues it.

Sound 6, queued at $10D5: set $30CA = $FE and $314D = 19; noise at $1000, AD $DB SR $FE; gate on for 8 ticks, off for 14, call $314F to count $314D down, and repeat while it is non-zero; stops early when $30CA = 1, then SR $08, gate off, wait 18 ticks.
Repeat counter for sound 6, set to 19 by the script at $3115 and decremented by the code at $314F.
Machine code called by sound 6's script (command $0A at $3137): DEC $314D, RTS.
Sound 23: set $3231 = $FE, noise at $1000 with AD 0 SR $20, gate on, then wait a tick at a time until $3231 = 1 (sound 11 sets it). Not queued by any High Jump code found.

Sound 7: set $30CA = $FE, noise at $2700, AD 1 SR 1, 32 repeats ($3199) of a gate-on note with release after 12 ticks and a 13-tick wait, counted down by $319B; ends early when $30CA = 1. No High Jump call found.
Repeat counter for sound 7: 32 from $3174, decremented by $319B.
Machine code called by sound 7's script at $3189: DEC $3199, RTS.
Sound 8: as sound 7 with noise at $4000, AD 0 SR 0, 40 repeats ($31CF) of release-after-9 and a 10-tick wait; ends early when $30CA = 1. No High Jump call found.
Repeat counter for sound 8: 40 from $31AA, decremented by $31D1.
Machine code called by sound 8's script at $31BF: DEC $31CF, RTS.
Sound 9, played through $2DB8 by $16A2 when the speed is high: subroutines $344D (triangle sweep), $339C (noise sequence) and $3351, wait 34 ticks, then $339C again.
Sound 10: three rising triangle sweeps, $1000 to $2780 by $02C0, $2400 to $3E80 by $03C0, $1800 to $5000 by $0480, then down by $0340 to $1000. No High Jump call found.
Script variable for sounds 12 and 23: they set $FE and wait for 1, which sound 11 writes.
Sound 11: poke $3231 = 1, ending the hold in sounds 12 and 23. No High Jump call found.

Sound 12: set $3231 = $FE; noise at $FC00 for 2 ticks, then one tick each at $1A00, $0300, $0238, $0170, $00A8 and $9C00; then noise from $0180 falling by 1 a tick for up to 43 ticks (cut short when $3231 = 1), gate off and 7 more falling ticks. No High Jump call found.
Sound 13: noise from $0600 falling by $0014 a tick for 18 ticks, AD $69 SR $D8, release 12 ticks after the start (gate timer 11). No High Jump call found.
Sound 14: noise from $0600 falling by $0020 a tick for 11 ticks, AD $47 SR $06, release after 7. No High Jump call found.

Sound 15, queued by ramp_bottom_sounds ($172E) when the skater drops into the lower ramp ($23 >= $E0) after entering phase 2: noise from $0600 falling by $001A a tick for 12 ticks, AD $69 SR $08, release after 5.
Sound 16, queued by ramp_bottom_sounds ($1739) when the skater rises above $23 = $F0 after crossing the centre: noise from $0400 rising by $001A a tick for 12 ticks, AD $75 SR $05, release after 7.

Sound 18: call $331F (limits $8000 and $5000), then up to 6 cycles of a triangle rising by $0900 a tick to the upper limit and falling by $0900 to the lower, calling $3334 after each to lower both limits; ends early when $3349 = 1. No High Jump call found.
Upper frequency limit of sound 18 (word at $331B/$331C), compared at $32FB; $331F sets it to $8000, $3334 lowers the high byte by 9 per cycle.
High byte of sound 18's upper limit, the byte $331F and $3334 change.
Lower frequency limit of sound 18 (word at $331D/$331E), compared at $3307; set to $5000 by $331F.
High byte of sound 18's lower limit, lowered by 9 per cycle in $3334.
Machine code called by sound 18 at $32E5: store $8000 in $331B/$331C and $5000 in $331D/$331E, preserving A.
Machine code called by sound 18 at $3314 after each cycle: subtract 9 from the high bytes $331C and $331E.
Script variable: set to $FE by sound 18 and to 1 by sound 17; sound 18 stops when it reads 1.
Sound 17: poke $3349 = 1, yield, end; it stops sound 18. No High Jump call found.

Sound 19, also called as a subroutine by sound 9: noise at $FC00 for 1 tick, noise from $00C8 rising by $012C for 3 ticks, $FC00 again, then a pulse note at $0500 (width $09C4) falling by $004B while the width grows by $0037, 8 ticks.

Script subroutine for sound 9 (called at $31D8 and $31E1): noise at $FC00, then one or two ticks each at $1A00, $0300, $0238, $0170 and $1C00, then $0400 falling by $00C8 for 4 ticks; its $09 returns to the caller.
Sound 20, queued at $1ADC in detect_turnaround when the sign of $4E changes: pulse at $1400, AD $14 SR $F7, width $0320 growing by $0020 a tick for 20 ticks, release after 2.
Sound 4, queued at $0CE0 when $48 has bit 7 set: frequency $2800, then the subroutine at $33FE twice, then falls into it: three short pulse notes.
Script subroutine: pulse wave, AD $14 SR $F7, width $0800, gate on, release after 2 ticks, wait 8, then return ($09).
Sound 21: yield, then lower the voice's current frequency by $0240 a tick until it is not above $2C00; then noise at $0180, AD 1 SR $D4, falling by 3 a tick for 59 ticks. No High Jump call found.
Sound 22, played through $2DB7 by $16A2 at lower speed: subroutine $344D, then noise at $0220 rising by $0050 for 2 ticks and falling by $001E for 25.
Script subroutine for sounds 9 and 22: triangle at $1000, AD $50 SR $F7, rising by $0280 a tick to $3800, gate off, falling by $01C0 to $0240, return.

Music phrase table, four bytes per phrase: the note-stream address for voice A, then for voice B. Phrase 0 = $35AF/$3A02, 1 = $3634/$3A42, 2 = $36B4/$3A82, 3 = $3748/$3AC2, 4 = $37D3/$3B02, 5 = $385A/$3B42, 6 = $38DF/$3B90, 7 = $3960/$3BDE, 8 = $3981/$3C2B. Entries 9-15 ($3491-$34AC) repeat phrase 8 and are never selected (the successor table holds only 0-8).
High byte of each phrase's voice-A address, read at $3526 into the operand byte $34FB.
Low byte of each phrase's voice-B address, read at $3539 into $350C.
High byte of each phrase's voice-B address, read at $353F into $350D.

Script subroutine that sets up voice A of the music: pulse wave (gate off), width $0258, AD $05 SR $A5, octave shift 1, note lengths 4/9/$3B/$13 and gate-off times 3/8/$3A/$12, then joins the note loop at $34DA.
Script subroutine for voice B of the music: pulse, width $0400, AD $36 SR $C7, octave shift 2, note lengths 9/4/$13/$0C, gate-off times 5/3/$0F/8, then the note loop at $34DA.

Shared note loop of both music voices: command $07 plays the next note of the voice's note stream, $00 yields, then jump back. The $FF at the end of a phrase returns from the setup subroutine to the caller in $34DF or $3505.

Sound 1, the High Jump music, queued at $19CE and $1A45: clear $35A8, $35A9 and $35AE, copy $35AB into $35AC as a seed, queue sound 2 (voice B), then play phrase 0 on this voice; after each phrase call $3517 to choose the next and play its voice-A stream, for ever.
Operand of the 'set note stream' command at $34F9 (low byte), rewritten by $3523 with the chosen phrase's voice-A address.
High byte of the voice-A note-stream operand at $34F9, rewritten at $3529.
Sound 2, queued by sound 1's script: plays phrase 0's voice-B stream ($3A02) through $34C5, then after each phrase calls $3530 and plays the voice-B stream of the phrase in $35A9.
Low byte of the 'set note stream' operand at $350B, rewritten by $353C for voice B.
High byte of voice B's note-stream operand at $350B, rewritten by $3542.

Machine code called from sound 1's script at $34FF when voice A finishes a phrase: run music_choose_phrase ($3549), then copy the voice-A address of phrase $35A9 from $346D into the operand at $34FA/$34FB. Returns A = phrase.
Machine code called from sound 2's script at $3511 when voice B finishes a phrase: run $3549, then put phrase $35A9's voice-B address from $346F into $350C/$350D.

Flip $35A8; on the call that makes it non-zero (the first of the two voices to finish), pick a random successor of phrase $35A9 from the 9-byte rows at $3C6C, retrying while it equals the phrase before ($35AE), then move $35A9 to $35AE and store the new phrase in $35A9. The other voice's call leaves $35A9 as it is, so both play the same phrase.
Pseudo-random byte for the music: shift-and-subtract step on $35AB with $35AC/$35AD rotated in; returns $35AB XOR $35AC.
Return a random number below A (A must be non-zero): take music_random and subtract A until the result is smaller. Used with the successor count at $3560.
Flipped between $00 and $FF by every call of $3549; a new phrase is chosen only when it becomes $FF. Cleared by sound 1.
Phrase now playing, 0-8, indexing $346D (times 4) and $3C6C (times 9). Cleared by sound 1, so the music always opens with phrase 0.
Scratch byte for $3549 and $3597: the successor count, then the chosen offset.

Random state byte of music_random ($357E), shifted right on every use ($358D). High Jump never sets it: file $0E brings $8F from the disk (side1.g64, read with the loader table), so the first music after a load always takes the same phrases; later runs carry on from its current value ($F1 in the play snapshot). Sound 1 copies it into $35AC.
Second random state byte, rotated left at $3587 and seeded from $35AB by sound 1.
Third random state byte, rotated left at $358A; not initialised.
The phrase played before the current one; $3549 refuses it as the next phrase, so the music never steps straight back.

Music phrase 0, voice A: note stream $35AF-$3633, 128 notes of which 0 rests, ending in $FF. Escapes set attack/decay, sustain/release. Note bytes: low nibble 1-12 a semitone, 0 a rest, bits 4-5 an octave shift, bits 6-7 pick one of the voice's four note lengths; $xD is an escape with operands, $FF ends the phrase.
Music phrase 1, voice A: note stream $3634-$36B3, 127 notes of which 12 rests, ending in $FF.

Music phrase 2, voice A: note stream $36B4-$3747, 92 notes of which 12 rests, ending in $FF. Escapes set note with explicit length and gate-off, note lengths, gate-off times, attack/decay, sustain/release, pulse width.
